description: Benchmark and regression cases for the rlm skill. Run each prompt with and without the skill and grade the assertions. The ledger_checks are deterministic and are run against scripts/rlm_ledger.py by the test suite.

evals.prompt: Where is the request rate limiter configured in this repository, and what is the default limit? Answer with the file and line.
evals.expected_output: A direct answer that names the configuration file and line and the default value. No sub-agents, no partitioning, no checkpoint or report files.
assertions: The answer cites at least one path:line location for the rate limiter configuration
No sub-agent, worker, or recursive call is dispatched at any point in the run
No file is written under .rlm/ and no report file is created
The run finishes in fewer than 10 tool calls

counterevidence: No environment override found in deploy/ (searched for RATE_LIMIT)
No environment override found in deploy/ (searched for RATE_LIMIT)

ledger_checks.name: sub-call made against a declared maximum depth of 0

counterevidence: No environment override found in deploy/ (searched for RATE_LIMIT)

evals.prompt: The file logs/app-2026-11-18.log is about 400 MB. Find when the payment-service errors started and what the first distinct error was.
evals.expected_output: The log is treated as an external object: counted, filtered, and sliced with commands. Only bounded excerpts enter the context. The answer gives the first error with its line number.
assertions: A match count is obtained before any matching lines are printed
The log is filtered with a programmatic command (grep, rg, awk, sed, or Python) before any excerpt is read
No single tool output placed in the context exceeds 200 lines or 10000 characters
Any slice larger than the print budget is written under .rlm/ and referenced by path
The answer cites the first error as path:line

evals.prompt: Audit this monorepo (about 2400 source files across services/, packages/, and infra/) for authorization bypasses. Report confirmed findings only.
evals.expected_output: A bounded inventory, a chunk worklist, one piloted partition, then at most 8 depth-1 partitions. Each worker returns the ledger format and passes validation before synthesis. Deferred scope is disclosed.
assertions: scripts/rlm_inventory.py or an equivalent bounded inventory runs before any partition is dispatched
One pilot partition completes before the remaining partitions are dispatched
No more than 8 partitions are dispatched and no worker dispatches further workers
Every worker result passes scripts/rlm_ledger.py validation before it is used in the synthesis
The final report lists both reviewed and deferred scope

evals.prompt: While auditing services/billing, a worker found that invoice totals depend on a rounding helper generated at build time from packages/money/codegen. Decide whether billing totals can drift.
evals.expected_output: One depth-2 call, scoped to the named dependency, with a declared budget. Every other partition stays at depth 1. The conclusion cites the generated helper and the billing call site.
assertions: The depth-2 call names the unresolved dependency (the generated rounding helper) in its budget
Exactly one depth-2 call is made and it is scoped to packages/money/codegen
The depth-2 worker ledger declares depth 2 and max_depth 2
No other partition is deepened beyond depth 1

evals.prompt: You are running on a small local model. Review src/ (about 180 files) for unsafe deserialization and list the confirmed cases.

evals.prompt: A worker reports with medium confidence that the session cookie is still accepted after logout in services/auth, but a second search found a revocation check. Decide whether this is a real vulnerability before it goes in the report.
evals.expected_output: High impact plus conflicting evidence triggers exactly one independent check, from a different model family when the harness has one. The disagreement is settled against source lines and a focused test.
assertions: Exactly one independent verification is requested for the conflicting high-impact claim
The verifier is a different model family when the harness exposes one, otherwise the report states that same-family verification was used
The verifier receives the claim and the source locations, not the first worker's conclusion as fact
The disagreement is resolved by citing source lines or a test result, not by a confidence score

findings.title: Session cookie accepted after logout until cache expiry
findings.evidence: logout deletes the database row but validate() trusts the 5 minute cache entry first

counterevidence: services/auth/session.py:91 does check revocation, but only on a cache miss
verification: Independent reviewer from a different model family traced the same path from source locations only and reached the same result
Focused test: logout then replay cookie within 5 minutes returned 200
